title: Invita — the FBI's fake company sting

scenes.narration: [serious] The FBI built a fake company just to catch two hackers.
Two Russian hackers, Alexey Ivanov and Vasiliy Gorshkov, had broken into dozens of American computers.
First, they stole credit card numbers. Then they asked for money to stay quiet.
So FBI agents made a fake Seattle company called Invita. They invited the hackers to job interviews.
In November 2000, both men came and showed off. They were arrested on the spot.
The twist? A hidden tool recorded every key they typed. That let agents copy their files from Russia.
Russia charged an FBI agent with hacking. Both hackers went to prison. The job interview was the trap.

facts.claim: Alexey Ivanov and Vasily Gorshkov of Chelyabinsk, Russia, hacked dozens of U.S. computers, stole usernames, passwords and credit card data, and threatened victims with demands for payment; the FBI lured them to Seattle for 'job interviews' with Invita Security, a company it created, where they bragged and were arrested
Ivanov stole about 3,500 credit card numbers from Financial Services Inc. of Glen Rock, New Jersey; the company, threatened with release of the data, wired $5,000 to a Moscow Alfabank account
Ivanov and Gorshkov were arrested in Seattle on November 10, 2000; Ivanov was sentenced to 48 months on July 24, 2003; Gorshkov was sentenced to three years on October 4, 2002
In Seattle the men used a computer with sniffer software that recorded every keystroke; agents used the captured passwords to copy nearly 250 gigabytes from their computers in Russia
Russia's FSB filed charges against FBI agent Michael Schuler for unauthorized access to computer information
